# Wiki Scaffold Files

Every scaffolded sub-wiki carries the same infrastructure files beside its pages. This lookup names each one, what it holds and who writes it.

**See also:** `wiki-conventions` — for how links between pages are formed and resolved.
**See also:** `wiki-tree-layout` — for which of these files and directories a page walk skips.

## Essential per-wiki files

Every scaffolded sub-wiki contains the files below. `/wiki-lint` Pass 1 flags missing or malformed ones.

- `index.md` — catalog organized by page type with one-line summaries, each type heading carrying the freshness threshold in effect. Product modules list beneath their type heading by deliverable kind, each deliverable followed by its areas, then the top-level `_shared` tree under `### Shared`; a module no top-level page reaches lists under `### Unclassified`. Engine-rendered by the wiki's scaffold step and by reindexing from the current page set; never hand-written, and `index-parity` reports it when it drifts. The LLM's query entry point.
- `_derived/cited-by.md` (wiki root) — the reverse citation edge: every page with the pages that cite it, each typed edge labeled with the frontmatter field it came from. Engine output, committed, never hand-edited; `cited-by-parity` reports it when it drifts. Read it for what cites a page rather than scanning the pages for mentions; when it is absent or `/wiki-lint` reports it out of date, fall back to scanning, and report the stale file with the result.
- `_derived/graph-<name>.{md,json}` (wiki root) — one pair per graph the engine derives from the pages: a Mermaid view and a JSON document each. Engine output, committed, never hand-edited; `derived-graphs-parity` reports one that drifts. Read the Markdown for the shape of what the graph draws; the JSON is the same graph for a program, and agent-kit's orchestration guide, § *Reading the derived graph documents*, lists the graphs and documents their keys.
- `log.md` — append-only chronological log of narrative operations. Format: `## [YYYY-MM-DD] <op> | <title>`, **one entry per line**, enforced by `log-entry-format` (`/wiki-lint` Pass 1, error) — two entries run together are invisible to every line-indexed reader of the file, including the ingest cross-check. Never edited retroactively. The `<op>` vocabulary is **open**: each operation that logs uses its own name, gated by its own `wiki.logging.<op>` key (`wiki-configuration` §Narrative-op logging), and a human writing a page by hand names the operation they performed. No check constrains the verb, because this is living content a person also appends to and an enumerated vocabulary would make an honest hand-written entry a defect. What is NOT logged is fixed regardless of the verb chosen: mechanical, reproducible-elsewhere results, and this is not configurable — lint's pass/fail counts live in the report directory (`wiki-configuration`), and reindexing's page/type counts live in the regenerated `index.md`.
- Page subdirs by type: `concepts/`, `entities/`, `sources/`, `comparisons/`, `decisions/` (ADRs in `engineering/`, DACI records in `governance/`), `synthesis/`, etc.
- `_archive/` — created lazily; holds moved-out originals, with redirect stubs at original paths.

Shared `_raw/` pool at `<wiki.location>/_raw/` — one per project, used by all sub-wikis. Shared `_authoring/` pool at `<wiki.location>/_authoring/` — the author-facing rules, framework-owned and refreshed on every run of the wiki's scaffold step.

**How the scaffold and reindex steps treat each file.** `/wiki-init` copies `log.md` only when it is absent and never overwrites it once created, because it is living content. It renders `index.md` on every run, as `/wiki-reindex` does, with the `AGENT-READONLY` marker. `README.md`, `conventions.md`, `_templates/*.md` and `_authoring/*.md` are framework-owned generated content, refreshed on every re-run to match the current agent-kit source with the `AGENT-READONLY` header retained, as any other deployed file is. `_authoring/` carries the lookups that declare `reader: author` — the rules a page author must follow, materialized where a human browsing the wiki reaches them rather than only at a provider-specific skill path — plus one generated per-type author guide under `_authoring/types/`. **Unlike `_derived/`, a consumer may leave `_authoring/` untracked:** `_derived/` is committed because it holds a cross-page join no single page owns, whereas `_authoring/` is a rendering of agent-kit source and of the templates, carrying nothing a reader could not regenerate, so its diffs are churn on every redeploy. `/wiki-reindex` touches no page and makes no `log.md` append.
